board.name: New York State Education Department, Office of the Professions (State Board for Medicine)

licence.title: Physician Assistant (licence and triennial registration)
licence.renewalDeadline: End of the three-year registration period shown on the registration certificate

ce.categoryRules: No state CME hour requirement found; statute ties renewal only to CE the Commissioner of Health may establish. Mandated trainings below apply.

topicMandates.appliesTo: all PAs, at initial licensure/registration and every four years

topicMandates.topic: Pain management, palliative care and addiction (PHL 3309-a)

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 3 hours pain management, palliative care and addiction every 3 years for DEA registrants

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: No written agreement filing rule found; supervision continuous, physical presence not required; up to six PAs per physician in private practice (statute)
practice.notes: PA performs medical services only under physician supervision within the supervising physician's scope (Education Law 6542). Statute sets 6 PAs per physician in private practice (no limit in hospitals); the NYSED PA FAQ still says four and is out of date.

prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 3 hours every 3 years (PHL 3309-a) for DEA registrants

facts.quote: Renewal periods shall be triennial and the renewal fee shall be forty-five dollars.

facts.value: First registration is three years
facts.quote: $45 First Three-Year Registration Fee

facts.value: Only CE established by the Commissioner of Health
facts.quote: evidence of satisfactory completion of such continuing education requirements as may be established by the commissioner of health pursuant to section thirty-seven hundred one

facts.value: Every four years
facts.cite: Public Health Law 239; NYSED infection control page
facts.quote: All physicians, physician assistants, and specialist assistants must complete course work or training in accordance with Section 239 of the Public Health Law
facts.note: Same page: 'at the time of their initial licensure/registration and every four years thereafter'

facts.value: 3 hours every 3 years for DEA registrants
facts.quote: required to complete at least three (3) hours of course work or training in pain management, palliative care, and addiction
facts.note: Same page: 'by July 1, 2017, and once every three (3) years thereafter'; applies to prescribers with a DEA registration

facts.value: supervision
facts.quote: a physician assistant may perform medical services, but only when under the supervision of a physician

facts.value: 6 PAs per physician in private practice
facts.quote: No physician shall employ or supervise more than six physician assistants in such physician's private practice at one time.

facts.value: PANCE required for licensure
facts.quote: You must pass the Physician Assistant National Certifying Examination (PANCE)
together with evidence of satisfactory completion of such continuing education requirements as may be established by the commissioner of health
facts.note: The only renewal condition the statute names is CE set by the Commissioner of Health. NCCPA appears only as the licensing exam (PANCE).

facts.value: Not applicable to PAs: NYSED's list of professions needing the one-time 2-hour child abuse coursework leaves out PAs
facts.cite: Education Law 6507(3)(a); NYSED child abuse training page
facts.quote: This requirement applies to: Chiropractors, Dental Hygienists, Dentists, Optometrists, Physicians, Podiatrists, Psychologists, and Registered Nurses

facts.value: NYSED PA FAQ still says four PAs per physician; the statute says six
facts.quote: a physician cannot employ or supervise more than four Physician Assistants in his or her private practice

board.name: New York State Education Department, Office of the Professions (State Board for Nursing)

rn.renewalDeadline: End of the three-year registration period; NYSED mails notices five months before expiry

topicMandates.topic: Infection control and barrier precautions (Education Law 6505-b)
Identification and reporting of child abuse and maltreatment
topicMandates.appliesTo: RNs and NPs at initial licensure unless exempt or trained in a NYS program

topicMandates.topic: Updated mandated reporter curriculum (intellectual and developmental disabilities content, Chapter 25 of the Laws of 2024)
topicMandates.appliesTo: mandated reporters (RNs, and so NPs), including those already trained; complete the updated curriculum by November 17, 2026. Anyone trained between 11/1/2022 and 8/31/2025 may take a 15-minute addendum.

topicMandates.topic: Baccalaureate in nursing within 10 years of initial licence
topicMandates.appliesTo: RNs first licensed after June 18, 2020 who are not exempt under 8 NYCRR 64.1 (NPs with a graduate nursing degree already meet it)

aprn.title: NP (Nurse Practitioner certificate with triennial registration, by specialty)

topicMandates.topic: Pain management, palliative care and addiction (PHL 3309-a)

prescribing.pharmacologyCeForPrescribers: None per cycle found; one-time 3 semester hour pharmacology for certification
prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 3 hours every 3 years for DEA registrants (PHL 3309-a)

practice.agreementType: collaboration (written practice agreement and protocols) until 3,600 hours; none after, through July 1, 2030
practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Before 3,600 hours: written practice agreement with a collaborating physician and written protocols, kept at the practice setting for NYSED inspection; physician chart review at least every 3 months; names posted. After 3,600 hours no collaboration requirement under the version effective until July 1, 2030; from July 1, 2030 the statute text switches to collaborative relationships documented on an attestation form and protocols filed within 90 days

facts.quote: Every three years you must renew your NP registration and your RN registration with NYSED to continue practicing as an NP.

facts.value: NP registration coterminous with RN registration
facts.quote: Registration under this section shall be coterminous with the nurse practitioner's registration as a professional nurse.

facts.value: Not required to renew; one of the routes to initial certification
facts.quote: You are currently NP certified by an acceptable national certifying organization.
facts.unverifiedReason: No primary source says national certification is required, or not required, for NP registration renewal. Education Law 6910 and the NYSED NP pages loaded name only the triennial registration fee and the RN registration. The cited page covers only initial certification (national certification is one of two pathways). Value false is an inference.

facts.value: 3 semester hours pharmacology (one-time)
facts.quote: completion of not less than three semester hours or the equivalent in pharmacology

facts.cite: Education Law 6902(3); NYSED NP practice requirements
facts.quote: written practice protocols and a written practice agreement with a collaborating physician unless and until the NP has completed 3,600 hours of experience

facts.value: No collaboration requirement after 3,600 hours, effective until July 1, 2030
facts.quote: practicing for more than three thousand six hundred hours shall not be required to comply with the requirements ... relating to collaboration

facts.value: Collaborating physician review at least every 3 months
facts.quote: patient records review by the collaborating physician in a timely fashion but in no event less often than every three months

facts.value: Agreement kept at practice site for NYSED inspection
facts.quote: A copy of the collaborative practice agreement must be kept at the NP's practice setting(s) and made available for inspection

facts.value: Every four years
facts.cite: Education Law 6505-b; NYSED infection control page
facts.quote: registered nurses must complete course work or training appropriate to their practice regarding infection control and barrier precautions
facts.note: Same page: 'every four years according to Section 6505-b of the Education Law'

facts.value: 2 hours, one-time
facts.cite: Education Law 6507(3)(a); NYSED child abuse training page
facts.quote: two hours of coursework or training regarding the identification and reporting of child abuse and maltreatment. This is a one-time requirement

facts.value: Updated curriculum due November 17, 2026
facts.cite: Social Services Law 413 (Chapter 25 of the Laws of 2024)
facts.quote: mandated reporters, including those who have previously undergone the current training, complete the updated training curriculum by November 17, 2026

facts.value: 3 hours every 3 years for DEA registrants
facts.quote: at least three (3) hours of course work or training in pain management, palliative care, and addiction

facts.cite: NYSED NP FAQ q.3; S3916/A4524 (2025-2026) still in committee
facts.quote: No. New York State is not a Nursing Licensure Compact State.
facts.note: S3916 (NLC plus APRN Compact) was referred to Senate Higher Education on January 7, 2026 and not passed (nysenate.gov via WebFetch)

facts.value: BSN within 10 years of initial RN licence, for RNs first licensed after June 18, 2020 (with listed exemptions)
facts.quote: shall attain a baccalaureate or higher degree in nursing within 10 years after being issued a registered professional nurse license
facts.note: Exempt: anyone licensed on or before June 18, 2020, and students enrolled in qualifying programs by then. Not relevant to NPs who already hold a graduate nursing degree.

facts.value: Those trained between 11/1/2022 and 8/31/2025 may complete a 15 minute addendum
facts.cite: Social Services Law 413 (Chapter 25 of the Laws of 2024); NYSED child abuse page
facts.quote: if you have completed Mandated Reporter Training between 11/1/2022 and 8/31/2025, you may complete a short (15 minute) addendum

facts.value: From July 1, 2030 NPs over 3,600 hours keep collaborative relationships documented on a NYSED attestation form instead of the current exemption
facts.quote: the nurse practitioner shall complete and maintain a form, created by the department, to which the nurse practitioner shall attest

unverified: NY state controlled substance registration for PAs and NPs: no primary source was loaded confirming or denying a separate practitioner registration (the DOH Bureau of Narcotic Enforcement site returned 403/404). Left null.
NP registration renewal and national certification: no primary statement either way (see the fact's unverifiedReason).
NY RN general contact hours: none appear in Education Law 6505-b/6507 or on the NYSED RN mandated training pages. No page states outright that no hours are required.

Whether PAs must complete the updated mandated reporter curriculum by November 17, 2026: PAs are not on NYSED's Education Law 6507 child abuse list, and Social Services Law 413's list of mandated reporters was not loaded.
The NYSED PA FAQ (four PAs) conflicts with Education Law 6542(3) as posted by NYSED (six PAs). Use the statute.
No 2025 or 2026 New York law changing PA supervision was confirmed. The web search budget ran out before a targeted search, and Article 131-B as posted by NYSED shows no pending change.

Checked NYSED PA and NP pages and found no mandate on implicit bias, human trafficking, HIV (beyond infection control), Alzheimer, suicide prevention, cultural competency, domestic violence or end of life for PAs or NPs.

corrections: NY PA: re-quoted the infection control and prescriber education facts word for word. The earlier quotes used ellipses, which loses context.

NY PA: confirmed NCCPA is not a renewal condition from the text of Education Law 6541(3) itself, replacing the inference. Confirmed PAs are NOT on NYSED's list for the one-time child abuse coursework.
NY NP: NLC non-membership now cited to NYSED's own statement in NP FAQ q.3 ('not a Nursing Licensure Compact State'), not just to a bill's committee status.
NY NP: nationalCertificationRequired=false downgraded to verified:false. No primary source states the renewal rule either way; the cited page covers only initial certification.
NY RN: added the BS in 10 scope (RNs licensed after June 18, 2020, with exemptions) and the 15-minute addendum option for the November 17, 2026 mandated reporter update.
